newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall with U.S., nervous market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall with U.S., nervous market.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower late Tuesday after being ruffled by a decline in U.S. Treasuries.
"The market is pretty nervous," said a trader at a local bank, pointing to worries over the soft U.S. Treasury market and insecurity over the direction of U.S. interest rates.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.17 to 126.20, while Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 slipped 1/4 to 90-1/8.
Another trader said players are keeping their positions small in anticipation of key U.S. economic figures due later in the week.
U.S. February retail sales figures are due Thursday and producer price figures will be released Friday.
Considering the uncertainty over U.S. rates that has dominated in recent weeks, traders said the market is likely to continue in its cautious mode.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.13 percent from 6.18 percent.
